description: run.sh's json_escape() helper (added as the FIND-003 fix, run.sh:57-64) has two branches: a python3 json.dumps path (run.sh:59-60) and a sed-pipeline fallback for environments without python3 (run.sh:61-63: `printf '%s' "$val" | sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g' | sed -e ':a' -e 'N' -e '$!ba' -e 's/\n/\\n/g'`). The hostile-topic test added to tests/test-prop15-3round-abort.sh (lines 22-42) only ever exercises the python3 branch, because every environment this suite runs in (per its own python3-availability check at test-v05-real.sh:30 and elsewhere in the suite) has python3 present, so `command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1` at run.sh:59 is always true and the sed fallback at run.sh:61-63 never executes in any test run. The sed fallback is exactly the code path FIND-003 was raised to make safe (it is the ONLY escaping logic that would run in a hypothetical minimal/python3-less install), yet its correctness (that the two-stage sed pipeline actually produces valid, single-line, round-trippable JSON for a quote+newline value) is asserted nowhere — it is unverified code guarding the same JSONL-corruption failure mode FIND-003 described.

evidence.snippet:
json_escape() {
  local val="$1"
  if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    python3 -c 'import json, sys; s = json.dumps(sys.argv[1]); print(s[1:-1])' "$val"
  else
    printf '%s' "$val" | sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g' | sed -e ':a' -e 'N' -e '$!ba' -e 's/\n/\\n/g'
  fi
}
